speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The background and rationale for both Motions are addressed in this speech.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) is the main institution of the World Bank Group that lends to developing countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In October 2018, the Board of Governors of IBRD adopted resolutions to increase the capital of IBRD by about US$60 billion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IBRD intends to use the capital to support the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, more commonly known as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It does this, for instance, by supporting inclusive and sustainable economic growth through investments in infrastructure, as well as delivering higher climate co-benefits and focusing on crisis prevention.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a member of the World Bank Group, Singapore subscribes to the capital of IBRD.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bretton Woods Agreement Act (BWAA) governs Singapore's subscription.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are, therefore, seeking Parliament's approval to again raise Singapore's subscription threshold to IBRD.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I should explain that not all the amount subscribed to needs to be disbursed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The capital subscription comprises two categories: (a) Paid-in capital; and (b) Callable capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Paid-in capital is the amount that is actually disbursed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this case, out of the US$186 million, Singapore is only required to disburse about US$21 million to IBRD as paid-in capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The remaining US$165 million of callable capital will not be drawn upon unless in extreme circumstances, such as when IBRD cannot meet its obligations on borrowings or guarantees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IBRD is a triple A-rated institution with a long history of sound balance sheets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, the full increase in Singapore's subscription to IBRD’s capital will be charged to the Consolidated Fund, as the callable capital represents an increase in the Government's financial liabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IDA was started in 1960 and is replenished every three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Governments are due to pledge their contributions for the next three-year tranche from financial year (FY) 2021 to FY 2023 this December under the 19th IDA Replenishment exercise (IDA19).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IDA has been playing a leading role in helping the world's poorest countries by providing loans and grants for programmes that boost economic growth, reduce inequalities and improve living conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To support IDA, Singapore contributed US$46 million during the 18th Replenishment exercise in 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Structurally, IDA's replenishments comprise subscription and non-subscription components.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, Singapore's cumulative subscription to IDA since 2002 stands at US$1.09 million.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For IDA19, we believe that the majority of IDA donors are likely to support a total replenishment size of about US$82 billion over the period of FY2021 to FY2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will enable IDA to channel more resources to countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations; support programmes that prioritise capability building and economic transformation, as well as enhance crisis response and pandemic preparedness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The IDA Act guides our subscription to IDA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a result, we are also seeking Parliament's approval to raise the subscription threshold to IDA from US$1.1 million to US$1.3 million.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition to the foregoing, I would like to update and inform Parliament that Singapore has voted in support of the resolutions to increase the capital of the International Finance Corporation (IFC) by US$5.5 billion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IFC is the private sector arm of the World Bank Group.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will leverage the additional capital to mobilise private sector investments in developing countries, creating markets to advance sustainable development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore's present cumulative subscription to the capital of IFC stands at less than US$0.2 million.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will be fully subscribing to the 8,612 shares allotted to Singapore in this IFC capital increase exercise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This amounts to US$8.61 million and will bring our total subscription close to US$9 million.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The actual disbursement will be less than that, at US$7.44 million as US$1.17 million worth of shares will be allotted through the conversion of retained earnings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This subscription, however, is contingent on the passage of the Board of Governors' resolutions to increase the capital of IFC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Voting for these resolutions is open until 18 March 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These amounts will be spread over the next three years or more and will be met from the Government Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are participating in the IBRD and IFC capital increase exercises as well as the IDA 19th Replenishment for the following reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, it is important that we do our part as a responsible member of the international community by contributing to the efforts of the development institutions to alleviate poverty and boost shared prosperity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our final loan with the Bank was signed in 1975.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Having seen and experienced first-hand how timely financial support could accelerate development efforts, we moved from being a borrower to a donor and partner of the World Bank Group in the early 2000s.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are supportive of the World Bank Group's strategic directions for achieving the 2030 SDGs and are keen to join the international effort to supplement its resources to generate more targeted assistance to those in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, the presence of the World Bank Group in Singapore benefits Singapore and contributes to our growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Members may know, the World Bank Group has an Infrastructure and Urban Development Hub in Singapore.
